citations.review_text: Nice graphics and sound design. However, I'm displeased by the save points.

Checkpoints could be more frequent. It's annoying having to keep running halfway across the level. 
Gameplay is slow too, feels like they're trying to pad gametime with a slow character.

The whole design, animation, the atmosphere all great but that is not enough to distract from the awful mechanics and all around frustration this provides. 1.5 hours was enough to get me to stop playing. Ambigous checkpoint system that doesn't tell you when the checkpoints happen (there is a save icon but it doesn't indicate a checkpoint, and on the actual checkpoints it doesn't appear), which has you replay tedious parts of the game when you fall victim to the awful controls and plummet to yor demise. Game also features dead ends for some reason and first play traps, designed only to kill you off so you have to replay some section and know that the trap is coming. It could have been a nice, simple little adventure with a lot of charm like Inside, but apart from the visuals it did everythign wrong.

“I can’t see ♥♥♥♥”-level dark-game with depth perception issues. Nothing really creepy yet.

94% positive but only ~51% complete the first underwhelming chapter (less than one hour of gameplay); seems like another example of “Steam upvotes games they don’t actually play”.

Little Nightmares masterfully establishes an oppressive, unsettling atmosphere that forces players to navigate a grotesque reality from an incredibly small perspective. Every shadow feels heavy with hidden danger, ensuring that the pervasive sense of insignificance remains a constant, chilling reminder of the protagonist's vulnerability within this surreal, nightmare-fuelled domain.

Gangly, disproportionate figures haunt the corridors with their uncanny, bulbous features, creating a visceral sense of revulsion during every tense encounter. These unsettling enemies elevate the stakes, transforming simple stealth-based traversal into a heart-pounding struggle for survival against entities that feel fundamentally disconnected from a normal, human existence.

Perspective shifts frequently demand absolute precision, yet the fixed camera angles often obscure vital spatial information when crossing narrow beams. Accidental falls become a recurring frustration during these sections, requiring repeated attempts that occasionally fracture the immersion established by the haunting soundscape and the game’s brilliantly bleak environmental design.

Grabbing objects and interacting with the world can feel surprisingly awkward, as the controls occasionally lack the necessary fluidity for such a delicate adventure. This mechanical friction ensures that even mundane tasks occasionally become trials of patience, requiring deliberate movements to avoid triggering a lethal mistake or an unintended, fatal tumble.

Collaborating with gnomes during the downloadable content serves as a notable highlight, successfully shifting the tone from lonely isolation to rewarding, shared effort. These moments demonstrate how mechanical variety can enhance the narrative experience, proving that teamwork within such a bleak setting provides a welcome, if fleeting, sense of companionship.

Frequent crashes on the console platform act as a disruptive anchor, repeatedly pulling players out of the decayin…

This game is supposed to be scary. It wasn't. Not exactly thrilling, either. The gameplay was simple. The interactions were janky, The story was always on rails. The only challenges I faced were from the game's controls. And I loved it.
        If I were to describe the atmosphere, it would be moody. The aesthetic, it would be creepy-cute. The theme, it would be tragic. It's like if Tim Burton animated a fusion of Limbo and Hat In Time, and then sat it in the corner listening to Linkin Park and Three Days Grace until it was forced to engage in social interaction. If you have the bitter resentment from your childhood repressed so far into your heart that it's threatening to form a singularity, this might be the game for you.

        If that hasn't convinced you, I can go into the game's themes. This may constitute minor spoilers, but I really don't think that's a problem here. Your character is Six. She is a callous antihero with a troubled past. Prior to the game's events, she found herself in the Nowhere, a nightmare world whose residents are deformed monsters that love nothing more than to abuse and devour whatever children they can get their hands on. Now, people say the point of the game is that your character is helpless, but that's not quite true. Rather, your weak, fragile protagonist is best described as... [i] ruthless. [/i]
        When Six wakes up, she doesn't run from the danger; she [i] is [/i] the danger. Her power is in patience, cunning, and determination. She wants revenge, and to gain enough power to save herself. And gain power she does... But those who fight monsters become monsters themselves. In the end, is Six any better than they are?

        Only a sequel will tell. Except it won't. Little Nightmares 2 is a prequel that establishes just what kind of person Six really is. Little Nightmares 3 follows unrelated characters, with dubious quality. Very Little Nightmares is a mobile spinoff with little connection to our heroine's charact…

citations.review_text: game didn't told me anything (hints what it is about, how the controls work), just running to one side of the screen..

Little Nightmares is an overhyped milestone in the horror platformer genre and I can see why: with a big publisher like Bandai Namco, cross platform launches, Unreal Engine 4 graphics and an admittedly great art design and chilling ambient sounds, the game feels much bigger than it ends up being.

Because in reality, it is a short adventure only 4 chapters in length (with the comparatively brief fifth chapter just being a final boss fight), with each 45 minute chapter set in a different location and having a different theme, followed by three paid DLCs that have been made as a result of the main game’s brevity. The Enhanced edition offers higher texture resolution, reflections of Six in puddles on the ground, circular waves if she jumps into a puddle, and Six will leave footprints on the floor if her feet are wet.

But returning to the main game, it takes place aboard a ship of sorts, called The Maw, and you play as a little kid in a yellow raincoat called Six, who is a girl. Armed only with a lighter, your job is to, well, keep moving towards the right in this platformer. You have to jump, duck, run, drag objects, hold objects (some of them are keys that need to be found elsewhere in a room to unlock a door), hold and throw objects (e.g. onto elevator call buttons), sneak past monsters and flip switches.

The game offers nothing else, no puzzles to solve or any stopping and thinking required on how to best approach a situation. The chases are, in fact, the most annoying parts of the game because they eventually require you to avoid obstacles you can’t really see; invisible kill zones you can only guess based on the foes around you. And having to run, do a long jump (yes, there are two types depending on a press, or pressing and holding the jump button) and then grab and hang onto a swinging lantern while being chased and use that lantern to jump over an abyss and land on a platform you need to grab the edge of on the other side, can lead to frequent retries. The ga…

short and sweet butt get it on sale
This is good game on the puzzle but very short gameplay

My first horror game ever. Dark and creepy but weirdly cute at the same time, I loved it. The chase sequences kept me on edge the whole time. Only downside: it's pretty short. Still totally worth playing.

Little Nightmares is an absolute masterclass in atmospheric horror. It completely shuns lazy cheap jump scares relying instead on a deeply unsettling art style and constant creeping dread. The chase sequences are easily the standout moments running for your life from terrifying monstrosities triggers an intense mix of fear sheer panic and a massive adrenaline rush that keeps your heart pounding from start to finish.
Beyond the terror it shines brilliantly as a puzzle platformer. The environmental puzzles are clever the controls feel grounded and the visual storytelling is top tier. While the game is undeniably short and can be wrapped up in a few hours there isn't a single minute of wasted time or filler.
Short sweet and genuinely chilling a must play for horror fans who value rich atmosphere and intense tension over cheap scares.
muy bonito, la estetica es preciosa aunque un poco corto para mi gusto

They really nail it with the atmosphere. In the videos it may look innocent, but while you play, It can make you feel goosebumps every time you fail.
Short, amazing, and horribly beautiful.
Nice puzzles, small gameplay. Perfect for a weekend!

PROS
- Incredible atmosphere and environmental storytelling.
- Unique and disturbing creature designs.
- Beautiful art direction and excellent sound design.
- Memorable chase sequences.
- Clever puzzles that complement the horror.

CONS
- Relatively short experience.
- A few puzzles can be unintuitive.
- Limited replay value once you've finished the story.

VERDICT
Little Nightmares completely drew me into its strange and unsettling world. I loved how it trusted the player to interpret the story instead of explaining everything outright, making every new area feel mysterious and worth exploring. It's not the longest game, but every moment feels carefully crafted. Even years later, I still think its atmosphere and visual storytelling are among the best in the genre.

5/5

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the absence of dialogue and direct exposition, noting that the story and lore are communicated through the environment and visual details.

citations.review_text:
A Perfect Little Nightmare

Little Nightmares was such a great experience for me.

I honestly didn't know exactly what to expect when I started it, but I quickly got hooked by the creepy atmosphere, strange world, disturbing creatures, and unique art style.

Everything looks weird and almost cute in its own way, but there's always something unsettling about it. The game does a really good job making you feel small and vulnerable without needing to constantly throw jumpscares at you.

I also really like how the game doesn't explain everything. You explore, see strange things happening around you, and slowly start putting the story together yourself. It made me pay attention to the environment and wonder what was actually happening.

The gameplay is simple but really enjoyable. Exploring, solving puzzles, hiding from enemies, and figuring out where to go all fit together perfectly for me.

And the enemies are unforgettable. 😂 Some of them look strange at first, but once they start chasing you, they become seriously creepy.

I also really liked Six. She doesn't need a lot of dialogue to be memorable. Just watching her travel through this horrible world made me want to keep playing and see where her journey would take her.

The atmosphere is definitely my favorite part. The interesting Story, The sound, environments, creatures, and dark visual style all work together so well.

For me, Little Nightmares is one of those games where everything just comes together.

I honestly don't have much to complain about. I enjoyed the gameplay, the atmosphere, the mystery, the characters, and the whole experience from beginning to end.

Little Nightmares is such a great game. i love the creepy atmosphere, the unique art style, and the way the game tells its story without explaining everything. It can be really unsettling at time, but that's makes it so good.

This game deserves all the acclaim it has received over the years.

It’s a visually impressive experience, and one thing I really admire about it is that there isn’t a  lot of exposition to explain the story to you. It just kind of plops you down into the world and allows you to pick up details through exploration and context. 

This version (the enhanced one) actually comes with the 3 dlc packs released after the main game, these are collectively known as the Secrets of the Maw dlc. It was a really great additional story that links into the main campaign, just told through the perspective of another character.

Definitely worth buying.

If you would like to watch a play through of the game, you can find mine here:
https://youtu.be/dutf-NnMevU

You can even watch a play through of the dlc content if you like:
https://youtu.be/QwNKMWVJmr4

If you are so inclined, I would deeply appreciate you subscribing to my channel (it’s free). Thank you!

I watched others play this game a while back, and now there’s always a point in the year where I get completely obsessed with Little Nightmares. The entire world is just so good it's easily one of my top 3 games. The whole story and atmosphere are incredible, including the DLC. This game really knows how to tell a masterclass story without a single word of dialogue.

[b]Little Nightmares is an amazing horror masterpiece.[/b]
That doesn't mean it's perfect. There are some janky physics and frustrating glitches. Some puzzles or sections are a bit annoying to complete, since you'll have to die a ton of times until you figure out how to get through. 
But, with the bad stuff out of the way, this is an iconic 3rd person horror game. You view the world as if the characters were in some sort of "dollhouse", and you're looking from the outside. The controls and movement are decent, but sometimes the perspective can play tricks on you. There are puzzles, platforming, stealth and monster chases, and some mixes of these types of sections too.
The artstyle and graphics are really good. The atmosphere is creepy and the sound design helps a lot with it. The music is pretty good, it sounds "childish" in a creepy way. The monsters' design and sounds are very gross and they really do a great job with being memorable threats.
Your character, a girl named "Six", has an interesting story, that you'll have to see for yourself. The overall story of the game is very mysterious and raises a lot of questions, some of which are never answered. Now, it's a bit annoying to be left with so many doubts about what the story is about, but it's still quite enjoyable.
It's kinda short, if you know what you're doing. But if you want more, you can always get the [url=store.steampowered.com/app/640920/Little_Nightmares__Secrets_of_The_Maw_Expansion_Pass/]DLC[/url]. But I highly recommend playing the base game first, to get the best out of its story.
Overall, this is a very fun game, I love it a lot, despite all its flaws. It's one of those game worlds that, sometimes, I just want to revisit and play again.

Little Nightmares - hooked me from the very first minutes. You are thrown into a huge, cruel world where you are nothing more than a tiny child, and that constant feeling of vulnerability makes every moment unforgettable.

My love for this game actually started back when it was first released. I watched countless let's plays before I finally experienced it myself, and it has stayed with me ever since.

The references to Miyazaki's works are simply incredible. They blend perfectly into the game's eerie atmosphere and make exploring its world even more rewarding

What impresses me the most is that Little Nightmares barely needs any dialogue. Its atmosphere and story are told through the environment itself. From major, unforgettable moments to tiny photographs hanging on the walls, every little detail contributes to the narrative. Instead of explaining everything, the game trusts the player to observe, interpret, and piece the story together.

Little Nightmares is a perfect example of how powerful visual storytelling can be

PROS
- Incredible atmosphere and environmental storytelling.
- Unique and disturbing creature designs.
- Beautiful art direction and excellent sound design.
- Memorable chase sequences.
- Clever puzzles that complement the horror.

CONS
- Relatively short experience.
- A few puzzles can be unintuitive.
- Limited replay value once you've finished the story.

VERDICT
Little Nightmares completely drew me into its strange and unsettling world. I loved how it trusted the player to interpret the story instead of explaining everything outright, making every new area feel mysterious and worth exploring. It's not the longest game, but every moment feels carefully crafted. Even years later, I still think its atmosphere and visual storytelling are among the best in the genre.

5/5

This game looked great on the outside but doesn't deliver, and I really had to push through to complete it (13 hours on steam deck)

Basically.. There is no story. You're just moving from room to room, with no goal nor freedom to explore. It starts quickly to feel like a simulator. Parts of the game just looked like the bath house in Spirited Away, even the 'monsters'. 

Okay so no story, but how does it feel playing the game? 
The rooms you're escaping are simple, you'll either find an exit or find that one item you can interact with, and then you're done. There isn't much thinking to it, I wouldn't even call it a puzzle.
Escaping enemies is as shallow, there is not much timing involved nor freedom. Stealth does not matter, the enemy will notice you regardless. I tested this by being loud and running versus stealth, and there were no differences.

Lastly the controls felt bad. The game is tagged as 2.5D which is incorrect, you're also moving beyond X and Y, which was extremely tedious because it is difficult to see where you're going. 

Your money is better spend elsewhere.. If you are looking for a puzzle platformer with horror, INSIDE is highly recommended

Throughout my playthrough I had mixed feelings about Little Nightmares. It has a lot of the puzzle platformer elements that I enjoy and the atmosphere is great. Unfortunately, I think that the gameplay and presentation are sometimes at odds with each other which can lead to frustration. 

Little Nightmares gives the player very little exposition right from the start. It drops you into a creepy inhospitable world where everything seems dark, damp and dirty. There's a few minor cutscene type moments but no exposition. Most of the storytelling and lore just comes from the gameplay and the environment. The scenarios you end up in paint an intentionally blurry picture of the goings on in this world. It's very imaginative and left me wondering about where I actually was, who the inhabitants truly were, and where Six, the player character, came from. This was a big driving force behind me wanting to complete the game. 

While the gameplay and puzzles are relatively simple I found myself often frustrated with this part of Little Nightmares. The controls are a bit wonky and imprecise. This may be intentional as you are playing as a frightened child. In that sense it captures the right feeling, but it can make platforming and interacting with objects a chore. The foggy dark environments also make it difficult to see what you are doing or where you are going. This combination makes for a lot of unfair deaths, and aimlessly trying random things to progress. I don't mind trial and error but I need to be able to clearly know what went wrong for that to feel satisfying. 

Ultimately, I'm glad I played the game and I plan to play the sequel. For me the Little Nightmares world is morbidly fascinating enough to keep going. I just wish it was a bit tighter and easier to navigate.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls as clunky, awkward, or imprecise, leading to unintended deaths and difficulty interacting with objects.

citations.review_text:
At most, this is a purchase that should be made on sale or for free. Still, I’m not sure I’d even recommend it at that point. 

It is ASTOUNDING that this game has an overwhelmingly positive review status at times. The internet loves creepy things; that may be the only reason I can muster to explain the positive reception. And even then, it’s not scary nor is it *that* creepy. 

Gameplay-wise, it’s not fun and it’s not very entertaining. 

The controls and awkwardness of maneuvering are awful. You will find yourself getting stuck on objects and inadvertently missing walls, ledges, etc. very often. Frustrating, to say the least. 

The plot has something there, but it really isn’t done all that well. The themes are obviously allegorical, but too contentious and certainly too ambiguous to really quite put together anything of substance. I was left wondering if the plot was meant to be direct which, in that case, it just wasn’t good. Or, the plot was meant to be something deeper; it was too confusing in this case. 

I disliked the “puzzles”, if you want to call them that. Very simple, annoying, and a chore trying to get to the next stage. 

Visually and audibly, it is VERY pretty and sounds terrific. I did appreciate the sound and graphical design. 

You know that feeling where you are nearing the end of a game, and you start thinking “What game should I play next?” I felt that way during nearly the entire play through.

[b]Little Nightmares is an amazing horror masterpiece.[/b]
That doesn't mean it's perfect. There are some janky physics and frustrating glitches. Some puzzles or sections are a bit annoying to complete, since you'll have to die a ton of times until you figure out how to get through. 
But, with the bad stuff out of the way, this is an iconic 3rd person horror game. You view the world as if the characters were in some sort of "dollhouse", and you're looking from the outside. The controls and movement are decent, but sometimes the perspective can play tricks on you. There are puzzles, platforming, stealth and monster chases, and some mixes of these types of sections too.
The artstyle and graphics are really good. The atmosphere is creepy and the sound design helps a lot with it. The music is pretty good, it sounds "childish" in a creepy way. The monsters' design and sounds are very gross and they really do a great job with being memorable threats.
Your character, a girl named "Six", has an interesting story, that you'll have to see for yourself. The overall story of the game is very mysterious and raises a lot of questions, some of which are never answered. Now, it's a bit annoying to be left with so many doubts about what the story is about, but it's still quite enjoyable.
It's kinda short, if you know what you're doing. But if you want more, you can always get the [url=store.steampowered.com/app/640920/Little_Nightmares__Secrets_of_The_Maw_Expansion_Pass/]DLC[/url]. But I highly recommend playing the base game first, to get the best out of its story.
Overall, this is a very fun game, I love it a lot, despite all its flaws. It's one of those game worlds that, sometimes, I just want to revisit and play again.

very cool 2.5D graphic visuals, dark atmosphere and soundtrack... yet very clunky mechanics that made me wanting to crash and break my keyboard/controller from time to time. which lowers the gameplay value especially for this type of games.

and about the story, apart from being an emo rock music video that contains a small girl escaping from degenerate elders by being possessed by a supernatural entity in the end, i strongly think that this game simply points out the importance of birth control/contraception...
simply putting it, use condoms. a very high quality ones.

not recommended for the lack of gameplay value.

Throughout my playthrough I had mixed feelings about Little Nightmares. It has a lot of the puzzle platformer elements that I enjoy and the atmosphere is great. Unfortunately, I think that the gameplay and presentation are sometimes at odds with each other which can lead to frustration. 

Little Nightmares gives the player very little exposition right from the start. It drops you into a creepy inhospitable world where everything seems dark, damp and dirty. There's a few minor cutscene type moments but no exposition. Most of the storytelling and lore just comes from the gameplay and the environment. The scenarios you end up in paint an intentionally blurry picture of the goings on in this world. It's very imaginative and left me wondering about where I actually was, who the inhabitants truly were, and where Six, the player character, came from. This was a big driving force behind me wanting to complete the game. 

While the gameplay and puzzles are relatively simple I found myself often frustrated with this part of Little Nightmares. The controls are a bit wonky and imprecise. This may be intentional as you are playing as a frightened child. In that sense it captures the right feeling, but it can make platforming and interacting with objects a chore. The foggy dark environments also make it difficult to see what you are doing or where you are going. This combination makes for a lot of unfair deaths, and aimlessly trying random things to progress. I don't mind trial and error but I need to be able to clearly know what went wrong for that to feel satisfying. 

Ultimately, I'm glad I played the game and I plan to play the sequel. For me the Little Nightmares world is morbidly fascinating enough to keep going. I just wish it was a bit tighter and easier to navigate.

Charmingly beautiful yet horrifying at times for the faint-hearted, this game casts its spell on you from the very first scene! The story, design and gameplay are masterfully crafted, showing how a well-thought-out and well-executed video game can truly be considered a work of art! The gameplay is neither too long nor too difficult, making it accessible to casual players; and for those seeking an extra challenge, the collectibles and achievements are just enough to do the trick.

Let the clock strike midnight, turn off the lights, and press play!

Little Nightmares is a big gem that redefines the horror-puzzle-platform genre.
This was one of my first horror games and yet, even after years, I feel the need to come back to it. This is not just because of the breathtaking atmosphere and the engaging gameplay, but also because of the story's hidden meanings, which feel evermore topical.
The music is beautiful, the art style is so unique and the designs are quite grotesque. The puzzles are not too hard, but you can never truly turn your brain off, especially because there are constant threats that keep you glued to the screen and fill you with adrenaline.
As the name suggests, Little Nightmares reminds you just how unnerving it is to be defensless in a big and scary world, awakening your inner child to torment it.

citations.review_text:
After finally going through both Six's adventure and Runaways (DLC). Little Nightmares is a dark, unique and fun horror game. The world is huge and disturbing, yet keeps you wanting to carry on the journey as you unfold mysteries and encounter the revolting inhabitants of the Maw. (Beware of Granny. She's the worst!!!)

Had a few issues where some items and Nomes would get stuck and I couldn't pick them up, resulting to resume checkpoints. Camera and controls will get iffy at times when carefully climbing up/down obstacles or escaping enemies.
Keyboards alright, though console's probably a better experience?
Overall it's a great game series. Fantastic music score too. Worth picking up.

I liked the graphics and artwork of the game. It was a nice little adventure with the scenery of a nightmare, which is a preference for me. The villains in the game I thought were thought out and had some character and quirks to them. I found them really interesting to look at and I admire the details that went into creating them. There were times that I was spooked. I like that there were puzzles included in the game. None that I would consider difficult nor need for guides to complete. 

There isn't much of a storyline or any dialogue included within the game. I wouldn't recommend for children due to some scenes even though the blood and gore is limited in the actual gameplay, the background characters and surroundings remind me of animated versions of somethings that could appear in a gore, horror movie.

I like that little side quests were an option for players interested in completing them. Those were fun to look for and attempt. It is a fun adventure game if you are into dark and spooky places. Best played with a remote unfortunately, but it did make a difference as playing solely with the keyboard wasn't working for me as great. 

I can already tell you now that the OG Little Nightmares will be the best version, in my opinion, but I plan on finishing 2 and getting part 3 anyhow. I might look into the VR or the mobile game in the future. That is how much fun I had playing Little Nightmares 1!

Great game with great story with fantastic art direction. The gameplay is immersive at best, but infuriating at worst. Anyone who has beaten the game will tell you its got its fair share of bugs, oversights, and overall lack of refinement. I don't want to say lack of polish, because again, the visuals are mostly stellar.

Also, despite me doing just about everything on keyboard and mouse, this game is absolutely made for controllers. That goes EXTRA hard if you plan to beat the DLC

[h1]Little Nightmares[/h1]

[b]Little Nightmares[/b] is a creepy, atmospheric puzzle‑platformer horror adventure that drops you into a nightmarish underworld called The Maw — a towering, grotesque place full of oversized monsters, warped rooms, and the worst furniture you’ll ever meet. You play as Six, a tiny kid in a yellow raincoat trying desperately to escape a world that seems designed to eat tiny raincoats and smash their dreams.

[b]What works well:[/b]
• Atmospheric terror: The visuals, lighting, and sound design are top‑tier creepy — the kind that burrows into your brain.
• Unique art style: Beautifully grotesque environments mix adorable character design with rank nightmare fuel.
• Tight pacing: Story unfolds smoothly and keeps you hooked despite short runtime.
• Steam love: Still rocking a Very Positive review score on Steam years later — people dig this creepy gem.

[b]Some negatives:[/b]
• Short length: You can blast through the whole thing pretty quick — some players want more once they’re hooked.
• Clunky controls & camera: Platforming can be awkward, especially in tense chase bits.
• Puzzle simplicity: Some puzzles are too easy or vague, leading to walking‑in‑circles moments.
• No big scares: It’s creepy more than scary — no jump scares, just “oh God what is that giant hand?!” vibes.

[u]Overall:[/u]
Little Nightmares is a beautifully eerie, tension‑soaked horror platformer that’s more about unsettling mood and freaky imagination than monsters jumping at you. You’ll feel tiny, hunted, and strangely invested in a yellow raincoat’s fate.

[b]Final verdict:[/b]
A compact but unforgettable horror puzzle journey — atmospheric, stylish, and unsettling — perfect if you love creepy worlds and clever design more than grind‑y mechanics or long campaigns. Worth a play, and even another run to soak in the twisted visuals and quiet terror.
